render: For each worker profile, emit a FLAT dist/qwen-code/agents/agenticale-<name>.md (Qwen Code 0.28.6 scans only the Markdown files directly inside .qwen/agents/, never subdirectories). The file carries name 'agenticale-<name>' (agent names accept letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores; colons and dots do not), the profile's description, and the matching neutral task-contract body copied from skills/work/references/tasks/<role>.md (implement, implement-easy, and implement-hard all use implement.md; consult and consult-hard both use consult.md). Beyond that, the frontmatter depends on the role's model routing from the flat model config at build time (adapters/qwen-code/models.json by default, or the --models option): a value whose provider equals codex.providerPrefix renders ONLY 'background: false' plus an executor block (kind codex, the codex command, the base args, and -c overrides pinning the model and — only when the value carries a #effort suffix — the effort, passed through verbatim); the host rejects an external agent that supplies model (other than inherit), maxTurns, tools, disallowedTools, or related overrides, so none of those fields renders for codex-routed profiles. Any other listed provider renders 'maxTurns', 'background: false', the disallowedTools list rendered from the profile's permission policy via permissionToolNames, and one 'model:' line carrying the BARE model id (the provider component is routing information only; the host's authType:modelId form recognizes built-in auth types alone, and a bare id resolves the session auth type first, then built-in auth types, with custom-provider models reachable through their protocol bucket). An unlisted role (or --no-model) renders the direct form with no model line and no executor block, so the profile inherits the session model. The seven base roles always render, one profile per role; the optional implement-easy and consult-hard profiles render only when the config lists them explicitly. When the config carries the top-level coordinator key, the build additionally emits the flat coordinator agent file from the coordinator entry below (body copied from the adapter-owned coordinator.md); the coordinator value must be Qwen-direct — the build skips a codex-routed coordinator value with a console note and a state record, because the coordinating session switches to that model within Qwen's own provider registry and a codex executor definition never makes its model available to the session. Qwen Code has no session-primary agent concept, so the coordinating session adopts the coordinator body per the runtime binding.

profiles.name: explore
profiles.description: Focused reconnaissance of project or external source for one tightly scoped question.

profiles.name: implement
profiles.description: Implements one small, verifiable implementation slice.

profiles.name: implement-easy
profiles.description: Implements one routine implementation slice (easy-task dispatch context).

profiles.name: implement-hard
profiles.description: Implements one reasoning-heavy implementation slice (hard-task dispatch context).

profiles.name: fix
profiles.description: Addresses only the specified review findings in a fix pass.

profiles.name: review
profiles.description: Independent high-reasoning review of one completed implementation slice.

profiles.name: review-deep
profiles.description: Expensive, integration-level audit of several accepted implementation slices.

profiles.name: consult
profiles.description: Independent second opinion on one stuck technical decision; read-only, returns one recommendation.

profiles.name: consult-hard
profiles.description: Independent second opinion on one reasoning-heavy stuck technical decision; read-only, returns one recommendation.

coordinator.description: Workflow coordinator session that plans bounded slices, dispatches worker children, and integrates their reports.
